missing_ops.name: geometry.rowwise_distance
missing_ops.what: a distance between paired rows of two (n, d) matrices; the library only has distances within one matrix and cosine_to / distance_to against one reference vector

missing_ops.name: stats.significance_tests and stats.p_values
missing_ops.what: no operator for a two-sample t test, an F test, a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, a boxplot outlier rule or a 3-sigma rule, and no p-value helper: an incomplete beta had to be implemented by hand, so any method that ports Alg. 4 pays the same ~95 lines

missing_runtime.what: no client-side stage after SERVER_RECEIVE and no way to move this round uploads to a client: every client stage runs before the uploads exist, the only two-way exchange (CLIENT_ANNOUNCE / SERVER_EXCHANGE) happens before local training, a server outbox is carried with the next round broadcast, and the channel cannot hold n LoRA states anyway (messages <= 64 KiB, attachments are one flat tensor dict <= 64 MiB)
missing_runtime.blocks: S3, and with it the paper placement of the validation (S4-S13) inside the client enclaves; votes produced in the next round would be about last round models, so the round-independent filtering before aggregation cannot be scheduled

missing_runtime.what: data is a client-side kind and sample labels are not a kind at all: DataView exposes hashes, source tags and lengths and its raw samples are opaque, so the server can read no client validation set
missing_runtime.blocks: S4 and S7 on the server unless the deployment hands in a labelled set as a resource, which this port does

missing_runtime.what: the server-side model_handle is optional and the shipped server adapter offers ProbeView.score only (OpenFedLLMGuard(probe=...), HFProbe); the lora() and activations() of ModelHandle are not part of it, and a default server has no model
missing_runtime.blocks: S4 in every deployment that does not supply a full server-side ModelHandle; without one the plugin records a LookupError

missing_runtime.what: no attestation, enclave or secure-memory notion exists in the library
missing_runtime.blocks: S1 (outside the plugin anyway); the paper threat model (the server sees neither client data nor honest votes) is not enforceable here

deviations: Validation runs on the server over one defender-held labelled set, not inside each client TEE over that client own data: the library cannot deliver the round uploads to the clients nor client data to the server, so the n client validators are replayed on the server (each upload is the reference model in turn) and only the data source and the place of computation change.
A model is a LoRA state loaded on the base model of the handle, not a full DNN upload; the DLO stage is one ModelHandle.activations call per state.

Deep layer outputs are the pooled submodule outputs the handle exposes (pool mean, every submodule selected), not per-token layer outputs of a fixed image architecture; which layers enter HLBIM depends on the deployment handle.

The forward cost is n + 1 passes over one shared set per round instead of n * (n + 1) passes spread over n clients with different local sets: the total compute is about n times smaller and centralized.
The votes are computed by the plugin instead of arriving from untrusted clients, so the robustness of the Alg. 3 stacked clustering against lying validators is not exercised.

The filter acts on the round uploads through Decision.excluded and the survivors get weight 1 (equal-weight FedAvg, delta 1); the host performs the averaging and the broadcast, so only the weighting of S16 is the plugin part.
S1 (TEE setup and remote attestation) and S2 (encrypted uplink) are not implemented: they are the protocol and the host, not a plugin.
Sample labels come with the validation resource rather than from the local dataset of each client.
Nothing here reproduces the paper numbers (CIFAR-10, ResNet-18, 20 clients, 2560 samples, PDR 0.1, PMR 0.45): the tests are mechanism only.
open_choices: The first principal component comes from fedguard.ops.transform.pca (centered SVD, library sign convention).
Alg. 4 line 11 splits upper and lower by the sign of the principal component value; the alternative reading (sign of value - median) differs only by the same shift of both groups.
The F test of Alg. 4 line 19 is implemented instead of the Levene test named in footnote 10, and it is two-sided.
The boxplot rule is 1.5 IQR; the 3-sigma interval is two-sided with the population standard deviation.
A test with degenerate input (fewer than two points on a side, zero variance) is skipped rather than fired.
The labelwise mean is the arithmetic mean; labels are ordered by repr; a label with no sample cannot occur because the labels come with the resource.
HLBIM features are label-major then layer name; only labels and layers present for every model are used.
A validator skips its own model and its own vote stays 1 (footnote 15), so the HLBIM matrix has n - 1 rows.
The cosine and the Euclidean analyses are independent and a model flagged by either is voted malicious (footnote 7 does not say how the two write the one vote array).

Agglomerative clustering uses average linkage on Euclidean distances of the values, in the pruning loop and on the vote matrix; DBSCAN uses Euclidean distance (with eps 0.5 this groups equal vote vectors).
On a cluster-size tie: the pruning loop takes the cluster with the larger mean absolute deviation from the median, the vote layer takes the one with more benign votes.
The model dropped by the safe abort is the flagged one with the smallest principal component value.
Where the reference distance is zero the ratio is 1 if the candidate distance is zero too and 1 + candidate otherwise.
The whole resource set is used, with no subsampling (Sect. VI-C leaves the subset size open).
The plugin needs at least 3 uploads and at least 3 models to judge per validator, and otherwise reports a skip.
needs_from_authors: How Alg. 1 / Alg. 2 handle the row of the validator own model: footnote 15 says the client does not evaluate its own model while Alg. 1 line 21 needs its distances as the denominator; is the row absent, constant, or evaluated?
The PCA behind Alg. 2 line 14: centering/standardization, solver, and the sign convention of the first component.
Alg. 4 line 11: are upper and lower split on the raw PC value or on value - median?
Alg. 4: F-test or Levene (line 19 vs footnote 10), the boxplot multiplier, the sidedness of the 3-sigma interval, and whether the p-values are one- or two-sided.
The shape of HLBIM after the label concatenation (Alg. 1 line 25 and footnote 8 vs the models x layers sentence in the text) and the concatenation order.
What a DLO is in their code: flattened or pooled, normalized, and whether the final classification layer is included.
How the cosine and the Euclidean analyses write the one vote array (footnote 7 vs Alg. 2 line 6): union, intersection, or one of them only?
The distance metric and linkage of the agglomerative clustering, and the metric of DBSCAN on binary vote vectors.
The definition of MIN(malicious_models) in the safe abort of Alg. 2 line 24 (smallest PC value, or closest to the median?).
Whether Eq. 1 divides by the number of remaining models after the rejected ones are removed.
confidence_reason: The detection mathematics, the iterative pruning, the stacked-clustering vote aggregation and the filtering run end to end and the three mechanism tests pass against the harness with a stub handle; but the paper placement (client TEE validation on each client own data) is replaced by a server-side replay over a defender-held labelled set, the DLO semantics depend on the deployment ModelHandle, and about a dozen Alg. 2 / Alg. 4 details are unspecified, so this is not equivalent to the authors implementation.
